name: Wernicke's area
summary: The posterior part of the superior temporal gyrus and the planum temporale of the dominant hemisphere, wrapping onto the supramarginal gyrus. It converts the sounds processed by the adjacent auditory cortex into words and meaning and sends the plan for spoken output forward to Broca's area through the arcuate fasciculus. Its destruction, usually by an inferior division MCA infarct, produces fluent but empty speech full of paraphasias and neologisms, with impaired comprehension and repetition, and often no weakness, so the patient may be mistaken for confused or psychotic.

anatomy.location: Posterior third of the superior temporal gyrus and the planum temporale of the dominant (usually left) hemisphere, at the posterior end of the Sylvian fissure adjacent to the supramarginal and angular gyri.

function: Comprehension of spoken and written language, selection of words for speech, and monitoring of one's own output.

bestView.label: posterior superior temporal gyrus at the end of the Sylvian fissure
posterior superior temporal gyrus and planum temporale

imaging.normalAppearance: Located on the left posterior superior temporal gyrus 50–60 mm from the midline, behind Heschl's gyrus and below the supramarginal gyrus; fMRI language mapping identifies it before temporal surgery.

pathology.finding: Restricted diffusion in the left posterior superior temporal gyrus and adjacent parietal cortex.
Left posterior temporal and inferior parietal atrophy, usually Alzheimer pathology.

pathology.pathology: Temporal lobe tumor near Wernicke's area
pathology.finding: Left posterior temporal mass; awake mapping needed.

lesionEffects.deficit: Fluent aphasia with paraphasias, neologisms and jargon
lesionEffects.mechanism: Loss of word selection and monitoring

lesionEffects.deficit: Impaired comprehension of speech and writing
lesionEffects.mechanism: Loss of the language comprehension center
The patient cannot monitor his own errors

examination: Comprehension: one, two and three-step commands; yes/no questions
Listen for paraphasias and neologisms in fluent output
pearls: Fluent nonsense with no weakness is a stroke, not delirium: check the visual fields and the clock
Comprehension of commands is the quickest bedside separator of Broca (preserved) from Wernicke (impaired) aphasia
